record.paper_title: Some open problems in low dimensional dynamical systems
record.original_question: For rational difference equations of the form x_{n+k} = (A₀ + A₁x_n + ··· + A_k x_{n+k−1}) / (B₀ + B₁x_n + ··· + B_k x_{n+k−1}) with nonnegative coefficients as specified in the paper, determine whether there exist periodic equations not equivalent to the five known periodic examples listed there.

evidence.quote: Problem 11. Are there rational diﬀerence equations of the form (12) that are not equivalent to the ﬁve ones given in (13)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider rational difference equations of the form
  x_{n+k} = (A_0 + A_1 x_n + A_2 x_{n+1} + ... + A_k x_{n+k-1}) / (B_0 + B_1 x_n + B_2 x_{n+1} + ... + B_k x_{n+k-1}),
where k ≥ 1 is an integer, the coefficients A_0,...,A_k, B_0,...,B_k are nonnegative real numbers (not all zero so that the right-hand side is well defined for positive initial conditions), and the equation is interpreted on the positive orthant (so that every orbit with positive initial values x_0,...,x_{k-1} > 0 is well defined for all n ≥ 0).

Such an equation is called globally periodic with period p if there exists a positive integer p such that, for every choice of positive initial conditions x_0,...,x_{k-1}, the resulting sequence (x_n) satisfies x_{n+p} = x_n for all n ≥ 0. Two such equations are considered equivalent if one can be obtained from the other by a Möbius (linear-fractional) change of variables y_n = (α x_n + β)/(γ x_n + δ) with αδ − βγ ≠ 0, possibly combined with a permutation/reindexing of the variables that preserves the form of the equation.

The following five globally periodic examples are known:
 (i)  x_{n+1} = 1/x_n  (period 2),
 (ii) x_{n+2} = (1 + x_{n+1})/x_n  (Lyness, period 5),
 (iii) x_{n+3} = (1 + x_{n+1} + x_{n+2})/x_n  (period 8),
 (iv) x_{n+4} = (1 + x_{n+1} + x_{n+2} + x_{n+3})/x_n  (Todd, period 6),
 (v)  x_{n+5} = (1 + x_{n+2} + x_{n+3})/(x_n) type Gumovski–Mira-style example (the fifth classical periodic case in this family).

Question: Does there exist a globally periodic rational difference equation of the above form, with nonnegative coefficients, that is not equivalent (in the sense above) to any of these five known periodic equations?
artifact.status_search_result: The classification of globally periodic rational difference equations with nonnegative coefficients remains an active research topic. Surveys on the global periodicity problem by Cima, Gasull, and Mañosas list the same five known examples and pose the existence of further inequivalent ones as an open question; no published resolution producing a sixth example or a proof of non-existence in the full generality stated has been located.
